titulo: Alphabet (Jan 2023): $61.5 billion buying back its own stock, about 12,000 jobs cut. Now the math.
descripcion:
From the archive: Jan 2023. Not today's news.
Alphabet, Jan 20, 2023 (Pichai, email to employees): "I take full responsibility for the decisions that led us here"
In January 2023, Alphabet's CEO emailed employees that the company had decided to reduce its workforce by approximately 12,000 roles. The buyback figure is from Alphabet's 2023 Form 10-K.

Same year: $61.5 billion buying back its own stock, 2023, company-wide. $61,504 million of stock repurchased during 2023, company-wide (cash flow statement, Form 10-K; the row shows 2021, 2022 and 2023).
The math: $61.5 billion in buybacks (2023) ÷ about 12,000 job cuts = about $5.1 million in buybacks per job cut.
This is a ratio, not a payment and not a cause: the total spent on buybacks divided by the job count. The $61.5 billion is Alphabet's stock repurchases for all of 2023, company-wide, from its 10-K. The cut is approximately 12,000 roles, per the CEO's January 2023 email. We are not saying one paid for the other.

The responsibility was full. So was the buyback. (Our take.)

Sources:
- Alphabet 8-K, CEO email (SEC), Jan 20, 2023: «The fact that these changes will impact the lives of Googlers weighs heavily on me, and I take full responsibility for the decisions that led us here.» and «We’ve decided to reduce our workforce by approximately 12,000 roles.» https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000119312523011424/d454494d8k.htm
- Alphabet 2023 10-K (SEC), Jan 31, 2024: «Repurchases of stock ( 50,274 ) ( 59,296 ) ( 61,504 )» https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1652044/000165204424000022/goog-20231231.htm
